assumptions: The founder remains employed and can devote roughly 20-25 hours weekly without using confidential employer resources.
The cited regulatory timetable and official-system requirements remain materially applicable to the intended customers.
No unprovided customer commitments, supplier data rights, channel agreements or validated economics exist.
A competent founder can use contractors for specialist compliance and geospatial review within the stated capital limit.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots from a narrowly defined commodity segment showing diagnostic-to-subscription conversion, realized prices, sales-cycle and CAC data, fully loaded delivery and support hours, retention intent, supplier cooperation rates, validation accuracy, and signed rights permitting durable reuse of derived evidence would support a higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: EUDR creates a real coordination problem around supplier documents, geolocation, validation, versioning and submission. The insight is useful but not unique: established vendors already address much of the same workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The dated regulatory obligation and buyer examples establish meaningful pain and spending on compliance software or implementation. They do not establish willingness to pay this prospective business, and free or inexpensive substitutes constrain pricing.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Onboarding plus recurring subscriptions could provide favorable cash flow and repeat revenue, but every material economic input is an assumption. Competitor prices challenge the proposed range, while supplier chasing, specialist review, liability, security and support could make margins materially lower than projected.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: CEE importers across several commodities constitute a relevant market, but the proposed initial segment remains broad across commodities with different evidence and operational requirements. The plan does not quantify an accessible, economically sufficient narrow beachhead.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Incumbents already offer supplier portals, validation, audit trails, ERP connections and official-system workflows, including demonstrated customer and supplier participation. The candidate has no owned data access, customer contract or exclusive channel from which to establish dominance.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful gateway could extend across covered commodities, geographies, suppliers and adjacent compliance workflows. Expansion is plausible, but each new chain may recreate supplier onboarding and domain-specific validation work rather than follow cheaply from the first beachhead.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: The proposed supplier-resolution graph could compound only if cross-customer reuse rights and durable supplier access exist. No such rights, exclusivity or revocation protection are established, and the official infrastructure plus source data remain externally controlled.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Polish-language support and managed exception handling may improve convenience for local importers, but no evidence shows a decisive improvement over incumbent platforms, consultants or the free toolkit. The offer's proposed pricing may also be substantially higher than public software alternatives.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The approaching 2026 and 2027 application dates, detailed data requirements and continuing rule and API changes create strong near-term urgency and maintenance demand. Simplification risk tempers but does not eliminate the timing advantage.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Customs-broker and ERP-consultant referrals are plausible, but there is no referral agreement, qualified pipeline, conversion evidence or measured CAC. Direct access to importer buyers is also not demonstrated, making repeatable acquisition a major uncertainty.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow pilot is affordable and document automation fits the founder, but operations depend on supplier cooperation, customer authorization and Commission infrastructure. Liability, domain review, security and exception support add demands that AI cannot fully remove within a part-time schedule.

highest_value_structural_change: Replace the unowned cross-customer supplier-graph premise with a narrow importer-specific contracted workflow position acquired through prepayment, explicit system access and a written operating mandate, while treating reusable data as optional rather than foundational.
main_structural_strength: A hard regulatory deadline creates recurring evidence and statement workflows that align with the founder's document-AI skills and can be piloted within modest capital.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is not presently owned or contracted: customers and suppliers control the evidence, the Commission controls submission infrastructure, and competitors already provide close substitutes.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Existing vendors already combine supplier participation, evidence validation, ERP connectivity, audit trails and official-system workflows at public prices below much of the candidate's assumed subscription range, while a free open-source toolkit substitutes for part of the readiness work.
